lab.name: MMBS Laboratory
lab.institution: Department of Chemical Engineering · IIT Kharagpur
lab.intro: We study how cells and tissues behave in engineered environments. Our work brings together microfluidics, biomaterials and biosensing to build laboratory models for studying disease and evaluating treatments.
about: The MMBS Laboratory is based in the Department of Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur and is led by Dr. Surjendu Maity. We develop lab-on-a-chip devices, organ-on-a-chip models, bioprinted tissues and sensing systems for biomedical research.

A central question in our work is how the physical environment influences biological behaviour. We combine experiments with computational models to study fluid flow and the movement of nutrients and drugs through small devices and engineered tissues.
Our research spans cancer, immune responses, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. We welcome collaborations with researchers in universities, hospitals, research institutes and industry.

research.title: Organ-on-a-Chip & Microphysiological Systems
research.summary: We build small experimental models of tissue and organ function to study disease and treatment responses under controlled conditions.

projects.title: Lymph node-on-a-chip for cancer vaccines
projects.description: A model of the lymph-node paracortex for studying how age affects immune responses to cancer vaccines. The published study used cells from young and older mice to compare antigen presentation, T-cell activation and responses against cancer cells.

projects.title: Glioblastoma-on-a-chip
projects.description: A 3D model that reproduces key mechanical properties of brain tissue to study glioblastoma drug resistance. Published work examines how pericytes, cells associated with blood vessels, influence tumour responses to temozolomide.

projects.title: Vascularised organ and tumour chips
projects.description: This research direction brings blood-vessel networks into brain and tumour organoid models. Work with collaborators at Duke University School of Medicine explores ageing, neuroinflammation and drug testing in immuno-oncology.

research.title: Lab-on-a-Chip & Microfluidic Technologies
research.summary: We develop miniature devices for biological analysis and screening, bringing fluid handling and sensing into the same system.

research.title: 3D Bioprinting & Biofabrication
research.summary: We use printing and biofabrication methods to make tissue constructs, scaffolds and customised microfluidic devices.

research.title: Biomaterials & Bio-interfaces
research.summary: We design materials for contact with living cells and tissues, with attention to how the surrounding structure affects biological behaviour.

research.title: Biosensors & Bioelectronics
research.summary: Our sensing work includes electrochemical and impedance-based methods for tracking biological signals, with an emphasis on integration into microfluidic systems.

research.title: Computational Modelling & Multiphysics Simulations
research.summary: We use simulations alongside experiments to understand microscale flow and transport, and to guide the design of devices and tissue models.

research.title: Cancer Engineering & Precision Medicine
research.summary: We develop tumour models to investigate the conditions that influence cancer growth and treatment response, with the aim of informing personalised approaches.

research.title: Drug Discovery & Immunotherapy
research.summary: We study how experimental models can help evaluate drug delivery, treatment effects and immune responses before clinical testing.

research.title: Tissue Engineering & Regenerative Medicine
research.summary: We explore biomaterials and engineered tissue constructs for studying tissue function and developing approaches to repair and regeneration.

research.title: AI/ML-Enabled Biomedical Engineering
research.summary: This research area explores data-driven methods for biomedical device design, image analysis and diagnostics.

people.name: Dr. Surjendu Maity
people.role: Assistant Professor Grade-I, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Kharagpur · Principal Investigator
people.bio: Dr. Maity leads the MMBS Laboratory. His research centres on microfluidic devices, organ-on-a-chip models and biosensors. He earned his PhD in nanotechnology and a master's degree in chemical engineering at IIT Guwahati, followed by postdoctoral research at the Terasaki Institute for Biomedical Innovation and Duke University.

timeline.label: PhD
timeline.text: Nanotechnology, IIT Guwahati, with Prof. Dipankar Bandyopadhyay. His thesis examined the transport, sensing and mixing of nanoscale objects in microfluidic reactors.

timeline.label: Postdoc
timeline.text: Terasaki Institute for Biomedical Innovation, Los Angeles, with Prof. Ali Khademhosseini. Research included organ-on-a-chip systems, cancer-vaccine screening and glioblastoma drug resistance.

timeline.label: Postdoc
timeline.text: Duke University School of Medicine, with Prof. Shyni Varghese. Research included brain ageing and vascularised tumour organoid models.

timeline.label: Current
timeline.text: Assistant Professor Grade-I in Chemical Engineering at IIT Kharagpur and Principal Investigator of the MMBS Laboratory.
